- dbe-tool sql "SET enable_profiling='json'; SET profiling_output='/home/shresth/dev/db_evolve/work/slots/slot0/.dbe/scratch_x.json'; <query>" then Grep '"operator_timing"|"operator_name"' in that file. /tmp is NOT readable. Put warm-up runs before the SET in the same call.

- Solved by E0021 (lineitem scan 37.9M -> 2.29M rows).

## Key finding: CM on join keys blocks the BF
- physical_hash_join.cpp FinalizeFilters: BF only if !has_cast && no storage_offset, except the E0021 branch: an exact BF through the offset on cond 0. A hashed BF is never pushed through an offset.

## Measurement lessons
- dbe-tool sql: the first 2-3 runs of a query in a process are slow (warm-up). Alternate A/B/A/B.
- Do NOT wrap in count(*): it changes the plan. Use a temp view + `from v`.
- dbe-tool bash: no pipes, no shell variables, no $(...).
- Bench noise is ±10-20% per template on identical code (q19, q08, q03, q14 worst).
- In long bench sequences q18 is ~10% slower after q09/q13 (a bench-process artifact, E0013).

## Profile snapshot (r6): q18 564, q13 541, q09 464, q05 260, q08 231, q17 227, q07 202, q03 197, q16 180, q19 165, q04 158, q14 156, q22 147, q02 80. Geomean 220.9.

- q13: inner agg on c_custkey 2.06s CPU (15M -> 1.5M groups). The large perfect HA is blocked only by the q18 bench artifact.
- q08: the plan head is all tiny joins; the big lineitem/part part was truncated. Check whether the part-key BF on lineitem is hashed (p_type filter ~13k keys over a 2M range = 150 bits per key > 128).

- CM join-key removal (E0017/E0018), HJ prefetch, agg run-collapse, in-place finalize, FSST heap reuse, dictionary filter, scan filter cost ordering, early HT grow, sparse perfect HJ, bitpacking select, BF on sparse perfect HJ, hashed BF through CM offset: ~0% or worse.
- Large perfect HA: real q13 gain (-20%), but the bench flags q18 each time. Possible retry: a shared table with striped updates, to shrink the memory footprint and maybe remove the artifact.
- FSST DecompressVector path is not hot (enable_fsst_vectors is off).

1. (dispatched r6) exact BF small-range floor (q17, q08).
2. If r6 helps: consider a floor of 2^23-2^24, or an exact BF for multi-key cond 0.
3. Extend the deliminator to ANTI delim joins (NOT EXISTS: q22, q21).
4. q05/q07/q03 not analysed in detail. Use the JSON profile trick.
5. q07: gate the offset BF when the scan already has a selective BF (only if q07 gets flagged).

## Codebase facts
- CM: src/optimizer/compressed_materialization.cpp + compressed_materialization/compress_*.cpp. In release, CM on a join fires only if est. build >= 1M rows and join/build ratio <= 8.
- Rule order: src/optimizer/optimizer.cpp (Deliminator runs before the join order optimizer). Scan-filter cardinality: RelationStatisticsHelper::InspectTableFilter.
- Deliminator: src/optimizer/deliminator.cpp (SelectionIsReplaceableByJoinFilter, ConvertNotDistinctToEqual from E0021).
- Join filter generation: JoinFilterPushdownOptimizer::GenerateJoinFilters (join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:232). NDF conds are skipped (:262). DELIM_GET build => build_side_has_filter (:330).
- Perfect HJ: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp:74. Perfect HA: plan_aggregate.cpp. FSST: src/storage/compression/fsst.cpp.
- Noise thresholds: q16 ~7.9%, q18 ~5%, q13 ~14%, q09 ~8.6%, q14 ~5.1%; q04 ~20%; q08/q17 ±5-15%.
- Budget is tight (~$4/session): read memory, the ledger tail and the profile head, then dispatch.

issues.title: Exact BF bitmap for small absolute key ranges
issues.hypothesis: q17 hot profile (JSON profiling, warm run): two lineitem scans take 0.77s and 0.68s CPU out of ~1.7s total. Each reads 60M rows and emits 368,435 rows through 'l_partkey IN BF(p_partkey)', but only 59,686 rows join, so about 85% of the emitted rows are false positives from the hashed BF. The build has 2,001 keys over range 32..1,999,954, which is about 1,000 bits per key. TrySetExactBloomFilter (physical_hash_join.cpp:893-941) caps exact mode at EXACT_BF_MAX_BITS_PER_KEY=128 bits per key, so the filter stays hashed even though an exact bitmap would be only 256KB. In q21 the exact mode cut BF scan CPU 0.83->0.38s (auto-memory exact-bitmap-bf-q21). The 128 cap existed to bound memory for large ranges, not because small bitmaps are slow.
issues.plan: In src/execution/operator/join/physical_hash_join.cpp, TrySetExactBloomFilter: add `static constexpr idx_t EXACT_BF_SMALL_RANGE = idx_t(1) << 22;` (512KB bitmap). Change the cap to key_cap = max(current key_cap, EXACT_BF_SMALL_RANGE), still bounded by EXACT_BF_MAX_RANGE. Keep everything else unchanged. Check that SetExactRange/bitmap allocation in bloom_filter.cpp/.hpp handles a range much larger than the key count: one shared allocation and memset, not per thread. Verify via JSON profile (SET enable_profiling='json'; SET profiling_output='<worktree>/.dbe/scratch.json'; warm the query 2-3 times first) that the q17 lineitem scans emit ~60k rows and scan CPU drops. If the ToString does not show the mode, compare scan output cardinality. Also check q08 (the part p_type filter, ~13k keys over 2M) and q02/q14/q19 plans for changed BF modes. Correctness: compare q17/q08 results and a sparse-key test (e.g. a 3-key build over a 4M range) against SET disabled_optimizers='join_filter_pushdown'.
issues.expected_gain: q17 -15..-30% (both lineitem scans, plus 6x fewer rows into two HJ probes); q08 possibly -5..-10% if its part-key BF is currently hashed; small gains on any query with a selective filter on a dimension whose key range is under 4M.
issues.generality: Any join with a small selective build side (filtered part/supplier/customer/date dims, DELIM_GET correlation keys) on integer keys with a moderate absolute range. This is common in star and snowflake queries. Possible slowdown: a 512KB bitmap probed randomly can miss L1/L2 where a tiny hashed BF fits in L1, so a scan that hits the BF with very few keys could see slightly higher probe cost. False positives drop to zero, which usually dominates.
issues.risk: Low. A two-line threshold change in already-landed, verified exact-BF code. Memory per BF is at most 512KB.
